subject: Shoply pre-launch: coordination for elevated 5xx/429 during traffic ramp
messages:
From: Sarah Bloom <sarah.bloom@shoply.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@shoply.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-launch smoke test -> sudden 5xx/429 spike (URGENT)

Marcus —

We kicked off a staged pre-launch ramp for Shoply Checkout (traffic ramp: 0 -> 10k rps over 30 minutes) a few minutes ago and are seeing a sudden increase in 5xx and 429 responses originating from the Redwood API path. Errors started ~10:03am PDT and are continuing; our frontend is seeing timeouts and customers are reporting payment failures in the staging flow.

Attached is a short summary of our ramp plan and a sample of client-side traces (shoply_ramp-summary.pdf). Key numbers:
- Peak attempted RPS: ~9.7k
- Observed 429 rate: ~12% of requests in last 5m
- 5xx spikes concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints

We need immediate triage and clear guidance on whether we should: pause the ramp, shift to a lower-concurrency config, or rely on Redwood fallback models. Our launch window is tight; this is high priority. Please loop in whoever you need.

Thanks,
Sarah Bloom
Product Ops 
Shoply

Attachments: shoply_ramp-summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Sarah —

Thanks for the heads up and the summary. I’m looping in Lauren (CS lead) and Evelyn (SRE/product on-call) for immediate triage.

Immediate asks while we dig in:
1) Can you confirm whether clients are using aggressive client-side retries? If so, stop retries for now (set to no-retry or exponential with long backoff).
2) If possible, throttle the client ramp to 2–3k RPS and hold while we check backend behavior.

Evelyn — can you look at the traces Sarah attached and tell us whether this looks like token throttling, queue saturation, or a new 5xx pattern? If we need a short-term mitigation we can flip a traffic router to a lower-cost model variant or insert a temporary rate-limit gate.

I’ll stay on this thread and coordinate.

—Marcus

On Thu, Sep 2, 2026 at 10:18 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sarah —
> Thanks for the heads up and the summary. I’m looping in Lauren (CS lead) and Evelyn (SRE/product on-call) for immediate triage.

Quick triage summary (initial read of attached traces + internal metrics):
- Root cause pattern: retry amplification + KV cache churn + a surge in long-context requests causing backend queue length to spike. Not a model crash, but a mix of 429s from token-service throttles and intermittent 5xx from queue timeouts.
- Correlation: High concurrency clients (short retry windows) line up with 5xx bursts.
- Impacted endpoints: /v1/chat (large context) and streaming /v1/generate.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now (can be applied in next 10–15m):
1) Apply a soft concurrency cap on the Shoply routing policy: max_concurrency=8 per-session (temporary).
2) Ensure upstream returns Retry-After header on 429s (we’ll enable for Shoply).
3) Flip to a slightly smaller model variant for staging traffic (same family, lower memory path) to reduce KV cache pressure.
4) Deploy an adaptive backoff recommendation header we can patch into the response to reduce client retry rate.

I’m attaching recent traces and a short log dump: redwood-traces-shoply-2026-09-02.zip (see errors/queue-timeout).

Next steps I’ll own:
- Apply the routing policy change and variant flip (target: 10–15m).
- Monitor 429/5xx after change and report metrics at +5m/+15m/+30m.

If Shoply wants us to pause the ramp entirely, confirm and we will open a brief maintenance window and coordinate rollback.

—Evelyn
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-traces-shoply-2026-09-02.zip (logs, 45MB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:40:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Pre-launch smoke test -> sudden 5xx/429 spike (URGENT) — MAP and timeline

Sarah —

Thanks for raising this and thanks Evelyn for the quick triage. Per our SLA and launch playbook, here’s a mutual action plan (MAP) we’ll execute for the next 90 minutes:

1) NOW (10:40): Shoply reduces client ramp to 2k RPS and disables aggressive retries (Sarah to confirm).
2) +10m (10:50): Redwood applies routing policy: max_concurrency=8 and enables Retry-After headers.
3) +20m (11:00): Redwood flips staging traffic to variant: rdw-medium-ctx to lower KV churn.
4) +35m (11:15): Joint validation window — Shoply submits synthetic transactions; Redwood provides 5/30/60m rolling error-rate and p95 latency.
5) DECISION (by 11:30): If error-rate <1% and p95 within SLAs, Shoply may resume controlled ramp to 5k RPS; otherwise we hold and iterate.

I’ve also attached a short config sheet with suggested client-side backoff settings we recommend (shoply-backoff-config.xlsx).

Lauren Bishop

Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick update from our side: we paused the ramp as requested at ~10:42 and executed the reduced-rps plan. Evelyn, the routing cap + variant flip reduced 429s significantly. We still saw some 5xx during long-context tests but well under the prior peak.

Outcome: after the joint validation window we are comfortable with a slow resume to 4k RPS with close monitoring.

One ask: the exec team at Shoply is watching the pre-launch and wants a short, named Redwood exec contact for the window in case the issue reappears during high-visibility testing tomorrow. Can you provide a single point of contact at director+ level?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will follow up on HubSpot ticket with logs from our side.

—Sarah
